title: Strongly graded commutative algebras are diagonalizable torsors
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $M$ a finitely generated additive abelian group, and $A$ a commutative $R$-algebra. Suppose $A$ has $R$-submodules $A_m$ for $m\in M$ such that every element is a unique finite sum of elements of $A_m$, $1\in A_0$, the image of $R$ lies in $A_0$, and $A_mA_n\subseteq A_{m+n}$. Put $B=A_0$, with its induced commutative $R$-algebra structure. Assume that for every $m\in M$ there are finitely many $u_{m,j}\in A_m$, $v_{m,j}\in A_{-m}$ with $\sum_j u_{m,j}v_{m,j}=1$. Then $B\hookrightarrow A$ is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] and of finite presentation as a ring map [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. For the group algebra $R[M]$ [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group], the $A$-algebra map
$$\beta:A\otimes_B A\longrightarrow A\otimes_R R[M],\qquad a\otimes b_m\longmapsto ab_m\otimes e_m\quad(b_m\in A_m)$$
is an isomorphism; tensor products carry their usual commutative algebra structure [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. In geometric terms, with spectra as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and fibre products as in [def-pc-fibre-product], $q:\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is affine, faithfully flat and finitely presented [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and the right $D_R(M)$-action defined by $b_m\mapsto b_m\otimes e_m$ gives an isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Spec}A\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}D_R(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Spec}A\times_{\operatorname{Spec}B}\operatorname{Spec}A,\qquad(x,t)\mapsto(x,xt).$$
For every ring map $R\to R'$, the natural maps $A_m\otimes_RR'\to A'=A\otimes_RR'$ are injective and give a grading with degree-zero algebra $B'=B\otimes_RR'$; the same hypotheses, conclusions and the displayed comparison hold for $A',B',R'$, with the comparison equal to the base change of $\beta$. The zero ring and the trivial group $M$ are allowed. No Noetherian, reducedness, torsion-freeness or finite-presentation assumption on $R\to A$ is made.

source.place: Tag 0EKK, label lemma-complete-reducibility-Gm, and example-Gm-on-affine supply the grading/action dictionary only. This strong-grading algebra theorem is an agent-formulated auxiliary, not the assertion of that tag; its full independent argument is retained in report.md. It supplies the affine quotient input assumed in Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Lemma 3.3.1(2) and Lemma 3.3.2.

proof.text: The degree-zero part $B$ is a unital subalgebra, and multiplication makes each $A_m$ a $B$-module. Write $a=\sum_m a_m$ for the given unique finite decomposition; the maps $\pi_m:a\mapsto a_m$ are $B$-linear, because multiplication by $B=A_0$ preserves every degree. Choose the assumed finite unit expression $(u_{m,j},v_{m,j})_{j\in J_m}$ for each $m$. Let $I=\{(m,j):m\in M,j\in J_m\}$ and let $F=\bigoplus_I B$ be the free $B$-module of finite coefficient families. Define $i:A\to F$ by $i(a)_{m,j}=v_{m,j}a_m\in B$, and $p:F\to A$ by $p(c)=\sum_{m,j}c_{m,j}u_{m,j}$. Both are $B$-linear and $ (p\circ i)(a)=\sum_m a_m\sum_jv_{m,j}u_{m,j}=a$. These formulas are finite because $a$ has finite homogeneous support and each $J_m$ is finite. Explicitly $F\cong A\oplus\ker p$ by $c\mapsto(p(c),c-ip(c))$, with inverse $(a,k)\mapsto i(a)+k$. Thus $A$ is a direct summand of a free $B$-module.

source.place: Agent argument from the stated grading and unit expressions; compare Tag 0EKK, lemma-complete-reducibility-Gm, for degree projections only.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat] to the direct-summand presentation just constructed: $A$ is flat over $B$. For a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset B$, if $1=\sum_l b_l a_l$ with $b_l\in\mathfrak m$ and $a_l\in A$, apply the $B$-linear projection $\pi_0$ to obtain $1=\sum_l b_l\pi_0(a_l)\in\mathfrak m$, a contradiction. Hence $\mathfrak m A\ne A$ for every maximal ideal, and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-faithfully-flat-maximal-ideals] proves faithful flatness of $B\to A$.

source.place: Tags 051G (lemma-local-artinian-characterize-flat, projective modules are flat) and 00HP (lemma-ff), (4) implies (1).

proof.text: Use the basis and Hopf operations in [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]. Define $\rho:A\to A\otimes_R R[M]$ by $\rho(a)=\sum_m a_m\otimes e_m$. It is $R$-linear, preserves the unit, and is multiplicative: for homogeneous $a_m,b_n$, both $\rho(a_mb_n)$ and $\rho(a_m)\rho(b_n)$ equal $a_mb_n\otimes e_{m+n}$; expand finite sums for general inputs. Moreover $(\rho\otimes1)\rho(a_m)=(1\otimes\Delta)\rho(a_m)=a_m\otimes e_m\otimes e_m$, and $(1\otimes\epsilon)\rho(a_m)=a_m$. Thus it defines the asserted right action. Since $\rho(b)=b\otimes e_0$ for $b\in B$, the two $B$-algebra maps into $A\otimes_RR[M]$ given by $a\mapsto a\otimes e_0$ and $\rho$ agree on $B$. The tensor pushout [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] therefore gives the $A$-algebra map $\beta$ of the statement, with its displayed formula.

source.place: Agent finite-sum version of example-Gm-on-affine; the Hopf formulas are those of the cited definition.

proof.text: The $A$-module $A\otimes_RR[M]$ consists uniquely of finite sums $\sum_m a_m\otimes e_m$. Indeed the coefficient map $[e_m]:R[M]\to R$ induces $a\otimes h\mapsto a[e_m](h)$, and these coefficient maps and the finite-sum map are mutual inverses, as is checked on a pure tensor by expanding $h$ in its basis. Define an $A$-linear map $\gamma:A\otimes_RR[M]\to A\otimes_B A$ by $\gamma(a\otimes e_m)=\sum_{j\in J_m}a v_{m,j}\otimes u_{m,j}$. The free coefficient description makes this well-defined; it is not necessary to assume multiplicativity of $\gamma$.

source.place: Agent construction of the inverse from finite coefficient families and the assumed unit expressions.

proof.text: For each basis tensor, $\beta\gamma(a\otimes e_m)=\sum_j av_{m,j}u_{m,j}\otimes e_m=a\otimes e_m$. Conversely, for $b_m\in A_m$, the element $b_mv_{m,j}$ lies in $B$, so tensor balancing gives $\gamma\beta(a\otimes b_m)=\sum_j ab_mv_{m,j}\otimes u_{m,j}=\sum_j a\otimes b_mv_{m,j}u_{m,j}=a\otimes b_m$. Every tensor is a sum of such homogeneous pure tensors, so both composites are identities. This proves that $\beta$ is bijective, hence an $A$-algebra isomorphism, its algebra structure having already been checked. Any choices of the unit expressions give its unique inverse.

source.place: Agent calculation; only the grading, the unit sums and the defining balancing relation of tensor products are used.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-subgroup-algebra-coset-presentation] with coefficient ring $A$, group $M$ and subgroup $L=0$. Since $M$ is finitely generated, it states that $A[M]$ is a finitely presented $A[0]$-algebra; identify $A[0]$ with $A$ by $ae_0\mapsto a$. The map $A\otimes_RR[M]\to A[M]$, $a\otimes(re_m)\mapsto ar e_m$, is an algebra isomorphism: its inverse sends $\sum_m a_me_m$ to $\sum_m a_m\otimes e_m$, and the inverse identities and multiplication law follow by expansion. Therefore $A\otimes_B A$, identified with $A[M]$ by $\beta$, is finitely presented over its first $A$ factor. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-descends-faithfully-flat] to the faithfully flat map $B\to A$ from step 2 and the $B$-algebra $A$. Its scalar extension is exactly this $A\otimes_B A$. Hence $B\to A$ is finitely presented.

source.place: Tag 00QQ, lemma-finite-presentation-descends; the group-algebra presentation is the existing subgroup/coset node specialized to the zero subgroup.

proof.text: Both spectra are affine, so [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine] makes $q$ affine. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine] and the flatness proved in step 2, $q$ is flat. The faithful flatness from step 2 also makes $q$ surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum]. Thus $q$ is faithfully flat in the scheme sense (flat and surjective).

source.place: Tags 01SH, lemma-morphism-affines-affine; 01U5, lemma-flat-characterize; algebra.tex Tag 00HQ, lemma-ff-rings.

proof.text: The single pair of affine charts $\operatorname{Spec}A,\operatorname{Spec}B$ witnesses local finite presentation everywhere by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], because $B\to A$ is finitely presented. Since $q$ is affine, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3) gives quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. These three properties are precisely finite presentation by the convention in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation].

source.place: Tag 01S7, lemma-affine-separated; the finite-presentation definition is the one recorded in def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation (Stacks Tag 01TP).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the source and target of the asserted geometric comparison have coordinate rings $A\otimes_RR[M]$ and $A\otimes_B A$, with their projections given by the two tensor inclusions. Under this identification $\operatorname{Spec}\beta$ has first projection $x$ because $\beta(a\otimes1)=a\otimes e_0$, and second projection $xt$ because $\beta(1\otimes b_m)=\rho(b_m)=b_m\otimes e_m$. Thus it is exactly $(x,t)\mapsto(x,xt)$. It is an isomorphism: apply the contravariant functoriality of spectra in [def-weil-affine-spectrum] to the inverse pair $\beta,\gamma$.

source.place: Tag 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes; the identification of the actual action map follows from its two pullback maps on rings.

proof.text: For any $R\to R'$, let $j_m:A_m\to A$ be the inclusion. The identities $\pi_mj_m=1$ and $\pi_nj_m=0$ for $n\ne m$ remain identities after tensoring with $R'$. Hence $j_m\otimes1$ is injective. Every $a\otimes r'$ is the finite sum $\sum_m j_m(a_m)\otimes r'$, so the images span $A'=A\otimes_RR'$. A finite relation among these images is zero only if each component is zero, by applying each $\pi_m\otimes1$. Thus they form the required direct grading, whose zero part is the image of the injective algebra map $B\otimes_RR'\to A'$; denote it by $B'$. Multiplication has degree sum since $(a_m\otimes r')(a_n\otimes s')=a_ma_n\otimes r's'$, and $1$ has degree zero. Each unit expression persists as $\sum_j(u_{m,j}\otimes1)(v_{m,j}\otimes1)=1$. No flatness of $R'$ is used.

source.place: Agent split-inclusion and finite-support calculation; Tag 0EKK supplies only the original degree-projection pattern.

proof.text: Finally identify $(A\otimes_B A)\otimes_RR'$ with $A'\otimes_{B'}A'$ by $(a\otimes b)\otimes r'\mapsto(a\otimes r')\otimes(b\otimes1)$. Its inverse sends $(a\otimes r')\otimes(b\otimes s')$ to $(a\otimes b)\otimes r's'$. For example, balancing by $c\otimes t\in B'$ sends either $((ac\otimes r't)\otimes(b\otimes s'))$ or $((a\otimes r')\otimes(cb\otimes ts'))$ to the same element $(ac\otimes b)\otimes r'ts'=(a\otimes cb)\otimes r'ts'$. Balancing over $R$ follows by moving its scalar to the final $R'$ factor. The two composite formulas give the identity on pure tensors, so these are inverse algebra maps. Similarly identify $(A\otimes_RR[M])\otimes_RR'$ with $A'\otimes_{R'}R'[M]$ by $(a\otimes e_m)\otimes r'\mapsto(a\otimes r')\otimes e_m$, using finite basis expansions. Under these maps $(\beta\otimes1)((a\otimes b_m)\otimes r')=(ab_m\otimes e_m)\otimes r'$ corresponds to $(ab_m\otimes r')\otimes e_m$, exactly $\beta'((a\otimes r')\otimes(b_m\otimes1))$. These generators span, so $\beta'$ is the base change of $\beta$. Step 10 verifies all hypotheses for $(R',A',B')$, so steps 1--9 apply to them. If $B=0$, then $1_A=0$, all rings in the comparisons are zero, and the spectra are empty; the formulas remain valid. If $M=0$, then $A=B$ and the comparison is the identity after the canonical identifications. No argument excludes torsion in $M$ or uses a finiteness condition on $R\to A$.
